Former Chancellor Angela Merkel Calls for Germany's First Female President

01 Nov 2026, 05:05 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily World Desk · Source: www.dw.com

Key takeawaysFormer German Chancellor Angela Merkel has publicly expressed her support for a woman to succeed current President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, highlighting that the country has never had a female head of state throughout its 77-year history. Speaking in a media interview,

Former German Chancellor Angela Merkel has publicly expressed her support for a woman to succeed current President Frank-Walter Steinmeier, highlighting that the country has never had a female head of state throughout its 77-year history.

Speaking in a media interview, Merkel stated that individuals should consider whether "it might finally be time" for a female president. While she noted that she is aware of capable women for the position, she declined to mention specific names. President Steinmeier is ineligible to run for a third consecutive term, and the Federal Convention is scheduled to elect the next head of state on January 30.

Potential Candidates and Discussion

While Merkel did not endorse individuals, several prominent figures have been mentioned in public discussions regarding the upcoming succession:

  • Ilse Aigner: Bavarian parliamentary speaker, backed by CSU leader Markus Söder.
  • Julia Klöckner: Bundestag president.
  • Karin Prien: Education Minister.
  • Annegret Kramp-Karrenbauer: Former Defense Minister.

Merkel characterized the ongoing discussion surrounding the presidency as unusual, pointing to an "unpleasant undertone." She also used the opportunity to comment on her own political home, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), asserting that the party's identity extends beyond economic matters and must focus on bridging divides across society.

Practical Implications and Verification

The presidential election will be conducted by the Federal Convention early next year. Observers seeking official updates on the election procedure and formal announcements can monitor releases from the German Bundestag and federal news outlets.

  • Role Context: The German federal presidency is primarily a ceremonial office rather than an executive governing role.
  • Timeline: The Federal Convention vote is set for January 30.
